newsitem.title: UK: More UK life insurers to go - Datamonitor.
newsitem.headline: More UK life insurers to go - Datamonitor.

text.p: Up to 20 UK life insurers could disappear with the loss of 7,000 sales jobs by 2001, management consultancy Datamonitor said in a report on Friday.

"Direct sales forces, the channel which received much of the blame for the pensions mis-selling scandal, are now paying for their role in it with a drop in new business of 25 percent in just two years," it said.
Investigations by regulators have found that thousands of people were poorly or wrongly advised to take out personal pensions from 1988 and many are still awaiting compensation.

"The legacy of the scandal and the cost of implementing tough new PIA regulations have heaped further problems on UK sales forces," Datamonitor said in its report "Direct sales forces and tied agents".
Regulator the PIA two years ago introduced rules governing disclosure of commissions and charges.
Only Prudential Corp Plc and mutual insurer Equitable Life have retained a strong presence in the market, the report added.

Many life insurers have found sales forces too unprofitable to run, with sixteen companies having axed their direct sales channels since 1992. Some 45 life companies remain in the market with 46,000 sales people.
Independent financial advisers (IFAs) and bancassurers are best placed to gain market share at the expense of direct sales forces, the report said.
